branchIdentityCreated.publicLabel: Alabama de novo circuit-court review after final agency denial

requiredFacts: AJIC challenge application and supporting official documentation were submitted
the original agency of record denied correction or removal
the written administrative appeal to the AJIC Director was filed
the Commission issued a final decision
the final-decision receipt date is known
selector.deadlineGate: File the agency notice and circuit petition concurrently no later than 30 days after receipt or service of the final Commission decision.

documentsInOrder: Notice of Appeal or Review from Final AJIC Commission Decision
Petition for De Novo Judicial Review and Appeal Under Ala. Code §§ 41-9-645 and 41-22-20
outputStrategy.costTreatment: Cite the statutory exemption from advance bond and advance payment of costs.

branchIdentityCreated.productOutcome: Prepare the bounded participant-filed notice, circuit petition, exhibit assembly, filing and service instructions only after verified exhaustion.

refusalConditions: AJIC administrative exhaustion is not proven
the agency disputes a material fact concerning identity, disposition, release or clearance
the agency contends that § 41-9-625 does not require removal of the particular information
a motion to dismiss or jurisdictional challenge is filed
discovery, subpoenas, witness preparation, live evidentiary testimony or cross-examination is required
bespoke legal briefing is required
appellate review beyond the circuit court is sought
the participant is seeking a general Title 15 expungement
the requested relief includes sealing or erasing court files

branchIdentityCreated.publicLabel: New York pre-November 1991 legacy sealing motion

selector.question: What is the exact conviction date?

branchIdentityCreated.outputStrategy: Generate only the motion theory selected by the exact conviction date, with proposed sealing order and proof of service.
branchIdentityCreated.productOutcome: Prepare an uncontested, records-based legacy motion and proposed order for the correct date cohort.

dateSpecificSubroutes.instrument: Motion for an Order Granting Relief Under CPL § 160.55(3)
dateSpecificSubroutes.noticeRule: Provide the full motion to the district attorney on not less than 20 days' notice before submission or hearing.

dateSpecificSubroutes.governedBy: former CPL § 160.55 through a motion to enter or enforce the omitted legacy sealing order
dateSpecificSubroutes.instrument: Motion to Enter and Enforce a Legacy Sealing Order Under Former CPL § 160.55
dateSpecificSubroutes.noticeRule: Serve the district attorney and follow the terminating court's local criminal-motion return-date and service rules. A 20-day operational minimum is not an express statutory requirement for this cohort.
dateSpecificSubroutes.requiredAllegation: State the historical failure to enter or transmit the sealing order required by the law governing the disposition.

refusalConditions: the district attorney opposes sealing in the interests of justice
a prior order directed that sealing not occur
the court disputes the procedural vehicle for the September 1980 through October 1991 cohort
the court requires a different successor-court or transferred-record procedure
identity, offense, disposition or conviction date is disputed
the potential CPL § 160.55(4) exclusion is implicated
the participant seeks sealing of the courthouse file rather than the agency records covered by § 160.55
an evidentiary hearing, factual investigation or appellate proceeding is required

branchIdentityCreated.publicLabel: Nebraska postconviction guidance and professional handoff
branchIdentityCreated.selector: A participant asking to overturn a Nebraska conviction is routed to neutral education and professional referrals, never to merits generation.
branchIdentityCreated.productOutcome: Provide deadline-sensitive orientation, records collection and referrals without selecting or drafting a claim.

guidanceOutputs: a record and transcript collection checklist
referrals to postconviction counsel, public defenders where available, innocence organizations or legal aid
information that appointment of counsel is discretionary rather than automatic
refusalConditions: stop before selecting, framing, drafting, verifying or filing any substantive postconviction ground
do not generate the merits motion
do not determine which constitutional claims to assert
do not decide whether a claim is procedurally defaulted
do not calculate prejudice
do not select a limitations exception
do not advise a participant to omit or reserve a potential claim

branchIdentityCreated.publicLabel: Utah Motion to Reduce Conviction under § 76-3-402
branchIdentityCreated.selector: Select exactly one statutory timing and eligibility branch; verify every consent-dependent branch from signed or on-record prosecutorial consent.

documentsInOrder: Motion to Reduce Conviction Pursuant to Utah Code § 76-3-402
Request to Submit for Decision after the response period
Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Order on Motion to Reduce Conviction

branchIdentityCreated.productOutcome: Prepare objectively eligible defendant-filed branches and refuse consent-dependent or joint-motion branches without verified signed consent.

branches.when: after successful completion of probation or parole
after successful probation or parole in a later case, five years from sentencing in the later case
after successful probation or parole in a later case, three years from sentencing in the later case
after an unsuccessful probation or parole discharge, five years
any branch where a two-degree reduction is sought
the offense is a statutorily defined violent felony under the applicable post-sentence branches

rows.consentEvidenceRule: A participant's assertion that the prosecutor agrees is not consent; require signed written consent or the controlling determination's permitted on-record agreement, and require the joint process for substantial assistance.

sourceIdentityBlock.reason: The final Utah Courts form number for the motion is unresolved and belongs to R4_SOURCE_IDENTITY_AND_ACQUISITION.
